endorsements.quote: We therefore recommend not exclusively relying on model-centric methods in medium- and high-risk clinical applications, but to always involve a human-in-the-loop where the outcome directly impacts individual patients.
Option 3: Selectively deploy, using algorithms where safe and deferring others to human medical professionals.

unlisted_practices: Defer individuals excluded from AI use over concerns of subpar model performance to an expert clinician to ensure an equivalent standard of care.
Use principled, quantitative algorithmic sample selection (data curation, uncertainty estimation, out-of-distribution detection) to identify samples on which model predictions can be trusted.
Match sample selection strategies to the risk level and context of the clinical ML application.
Externally validate ML models to detect silent failure on new samples or individuals.
Consider socio-cultural factors carefully when selecting samples based on biological determinants so selective deployment does not propagate marginalization.

screen.reason: This is a conceptual/perspective paper discussing generalization challenges and selective prediction in patient-facing clinical AI.
